correctness.rationale: The subgroup classification is complete: any subgroup projecting nontrivially to the prime-order complement has kernel intersection invariant under the irreducible action, hence intersection \(0\) or all of \(V\). Fixed-point freeness gives exactly \(p^r\) complements. Partner counts are then exact: every nonzero proper kernel subspace permutes with all kernel subspaces and \(G\) but no complement; each complement has exactly the four partners \(1,V,C,G\). Summing these counts gives every displayed relative degree and the global degree. The actual frozen verifier was read; it constructs three irreducible actions and directly checks all subgroup products. The proof, not the finite replay, establishes the universal result.
correctness.risk: The formulas rely essentially on irreducibility and prime complement order.

final_claim: For \(G=C_p^r\rtimes C_q\) with distinct primes, \(r\ge2\), and nontrivial irreducible \(C_q\)-action, every subgroup is a kernel subspace, one of \(p^r\) complements, or \(G\), and the entire relative subgroup-commutativity function is given by the displayed closed formulas; on nonzero proper kernel subspaces it depends only on dimension and strictly decreases with dimension.
